title: Number Quest Unit 5 · The Measure Shop (Explorer)

items.q: A bag of rice has a mass of 2 kilograms. How many grams is that?
misconceptions: used 100 grams in a kilogram, not 1,000
used 10 grams in a kilogram, not 1,000
changed the unit's name but not the number
items.why: One kilogram is 1,000 grams, so 2 kilograms is 2 x 1,000 = 2,000 grams. A bigger count goes with the smaller unit.

items.q: A ribbon is 3 meters long. How many centimeters is that?
misconceptions: used 10 centimeters in a meter, not 100
glued the numbers together instead of multiplying
items.why: One meter is 100 centimeters, so 3 meters is 3 x 100 = 300 centimeters.

items.q: Four ribbons are measured. Which ribbon is the longest?
misconceptions: compared the numbers before changing the units
trusted the number and forgot the unit
items.why: Change everything to centimeters first: 150, 200, 120 and 90. The 2-meter ribbon, at 200 centimeters, is the longest.

items.q: A film starts at 4:15 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it end?
misconceptions: never traded 60 minutes for an hour
added an hour and all 50 minutes too
items.why: Hop on the number line: 4:15 plus 45 minutes reaches 5:00, and 5 minutes more lands on 5:05.

items.q: Soccer practice goes from 3:40 to 5:10. How long is practice?
misconceptions: took the minutes away and forgot the hour
items.why: From 3:40 to 4:40 is one hour, and from 4:40 to 5:10 is 30 minutes more: 1 hour 30 minutes in all.

items.q: A bus leaves at 9:25. The ride takes 35 minutes. When does the bus arrive?
misconceptions: never traded 60 minutes for an hour
items.why: 9:25 plus 35 minutes: 25 minutes reaches 9:50, and the last 10 minutes cross the hour to 10:00.

items.q: A toy costs 65 cents. You pay with 100 cents. How much change do you get?
misconceptions: stopped at the wrong ten while counting up
added the price to the money instead of finding the gap
items.why: Change is the gap between 65 and 100. Count up: 65 to 70 is 5, and 70 to 100 is 30, so the change is 35 cents.

items.q: Nia has 3 quarters. How many cents does she have?
misconceptions: counted each quarter as a dime
rounded up to a whole dollar
items.why: A quarter is worth 25 cents, so 3 quarters are 25 + 25 + 25 = 75 cents.

items.q: A book costs $2.35. How many cents is that?
misconceptions: added a zero that does not belong
lost a dollar on the way
items.why: One dollar is 100 cents, so $2.35 is 200 + 35 = 235 cents. The 3 names the tens of cents and the 5 the ones.
